answer: A persistent identity accrues reputation only through slow, costly interactions, so a thousand fresh sybils each start at zero and must burn real work to matter. Idle identities decay: reputation is not a relic stored forever but a willow that bends and thins without tending, and a dormant fake offers no immediate leverage. A quill that stops writing loses its standing. This does not stop patient, well-funded attackers who farm reputations over months, nor does it detect collusion among established identities; it merely raises the capital and time cost. It also punishes honest occasional.
